title: Decide and apply pylint config tuning for convention-mismatch checks
description:
Once daz-mcp-server-wdk and daz-mcp-server-cpx land, re-run pylint with a properly-installed environment and the corrected version matrix to get an accurate baseline (locally verified at 4.41/10 as of this writing, see epic daz-mcp-server-lkb for the full category breakdown). Before working through the ~1500 remaining findings category-by-category, decide which checks are genuinely valuable for this codebase's conventions vs. which are structural false positives that should be disabled/tuned rather than 'fixed':

Strong candidates for disabling or reconfiguring (likely false-positive-by-design, not real defects):
- redefined-outer-name (190 hits): almost certainly pytest fixtures used as test-function parameters -- the correct, idiomatic pytest pattern, not a bug. Standard practice is to disable this check for the tests/ directory (or globally, since pytest fixtures are pervasive here).
- unused-argument (354 hits): likely dominated by two false-positive-prone patterns -- (a) @mcp.tool() function parameters whose signature is dictated by the tool schema Claude calls, not by internal logic, and (b) pytest fixture parameters requested only for their side effects/skip behavior (see conftest.py's live_client, figure_label, etc.). Needs a sample audit to confirm the ratio of real vs. false positives before deciding whether to disable outright or tune per-directory.
- missing-function-docstring / missing-class-docstring / missing-module-docstring (387+99+5 = 491 hits): a real decision point, not a clear false positive -- see the docstring category issue for the systematic-fix track if the team wants these actually written rather than disabled.

Needs real investigation (not obviously a false positive, don't disable without looking):
- no-name-in-module (158) / no-member (67): could be genuine dynamic-attribute patterns in dazpy/fastmcp that pylint's static analysis can't see (may need targeted # pylint: disable comments or stub files rather than a blanket config change), or could be flagging real bugs. Sample and categorize before deciding.
- broad-exception-caught (58): this codebase's tool functions deliberately catch broad Exception to route into handle_dazpy_error's typed-exception dispatch (see vangard_daz_mcp/_errors.py) -- likely intentional and correct given the design, but worth a quick confirm rather than assuming.

Output of this issue: an agreed .pylintrc (or [tool.pylint] section in pyproject.toml) checked in, plus a documented rationale (in the file itself, as comments, or in this issue's notes) for what's disabled and why -- so the next person touching pylint config understands the reasoning instead of rediscovering it.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/pylint-ci branch (commit bdfadcc). Investigated all four candidate categories by sampling actual findings rather than assuming: (1) broad-exception-caught (58) confirmed intentional -- disabled repo-wide via [tool.pylint.messages_control] in pyproject.toml with rationale comment. (2) redefined-outer-name (190) + unused-argument (354) confirmed ~97% pytest-fixture idiom in tests/ but with real hits mixed into src/ (e.g. daz_browse_category's unwired sort_by param) -- scoped both disables to tests/ only in pylint.yml so src/ findings stay visible for r13's audit. (3) no-name-in-module/no-member (225) confirmed NOT false positives -- real stale imports from pre-refactor server.py module path, same root cause as zp7; left enabled, notes added to ful for the follow-up fix. (4) missing-*-docstring (491) left enabled per the issue's own framing as a real decision, not a false positive -- tracked by dk7. Verified locally: src/ alone now scores 7.34/10 in isolation with the split config.

title: pylint.yml: install project dependencies before running pylint
description:
Root cause of the ~90+ import-error (E0401/no-name-in-module) findings that dominate the current 'Your code has been rated at 3.46/10' CI score: .github/workflows/pylint.yml's 'Install dependencies' step only runs 'pip install pylint', never installing the project itself or its runtime dependencies (httpx, fastmcp, dazpy). Pylint therefore cannot resolve a single third-party import anywhere in the ~137-tool codebase.

Fix: add a step (or extend the existing one) to install the project and its dependencies before the pylint step, e.g. 'pip install -e .' plus the dev tools currently declared under [dependency-groups] dev in pyproject.toml (pytest, pytest-asyncio, respx) since pylint also needs those importable for the tests/ directory.

Verified locally: reinstalling properly (uv venv; uv pip install -e .; uv pip install pytest pytest-asyncio respx pylint) and re-running 'pylint $(git ls-files *.py)' raises the score from 3.46/10 to 4.41/10 and removes the import-error noise, leaving the real, addressable findings visible (see epic daz-mcp-server-lkb for the full category breakdown).

Note: dazpy itself will resolve to whatever version is on PyPI (2.6.0 as of this writing) unless a specific version/local install is pinned -- that's fine for pylint's purposes (it only needs the import to resolve, not runtime behavior).
close_reason: Fixed on fix/pylint-ci branch (commit fc71ed6): .github/workflows/pylint.yml now installs the project (pip install -e .) plus dev tools (pytest, pytest-asyncio, respx) before running pylint. Verified locally: reran pylint $(git ls-files '*.py') in a fresh venv -- import-error/no-name-in-module noise is gone, score is 4.43/10 (issue's baseline was 4.41/10).

title: Infra: pyproject.toml, _client.py, _errors.py, _registry.py
description: Foundation layer for the refactor. (1) Add dazpy as an editable path dependency in pyproject.toml via [tool.uv.sources] pointing to ../daz-script-server. (2) Create _client.py: DazClient + DazScene singletons, async wrapper run_dazpy(fn) using asyncio.to_thread, and get_scene()/get_daz_client()/get_http_client() accessors. (3) Create _errors.py: map dazpy exceptions (NodeNotFoundError, ConnectionError, ScriptRuntimeError, AuthenticationError) to FastMCP ToolError with helpful messages. (4) Create _registry.py: extract the _REGISTRY dict and _register_scripts() logic from server.py. (5) Create tools/__init__.py that imports all tool modules so server.py just does import vangard_daz_mcp.tools. All subsequent module tasks depend on this one.
close_reason: Created _client.py, _errors.py, _registry.py, tools/__init__.py; updated pyproject.toml with dazpy editable dep

title: MCP Server Refactor: dazpy SDK integration + module separation
description: Refactor daz-mcp-server from a 15K-line monolith into a clean modular architecture. dazpy becomes the primary SDK layer (called via asyncio.to_thread); inline DazScript strings are the fallback for operations dazpy does not cover. The 128 existing tools are preserved; 11 new tools are added; the codebase is split into 14 tool modules plus shared infrastructure. See MCP_SERVER_DESIGN.md in daz-script-server for the original design spec.
close_reason: Closed

title: fix/pylint-ci: test_server.py's daz_save_scene_copy/daz_load_file tests silently hit a live DAZ Studio instead of being mocked
description: Discovered while verifying daz-mcp-server-ful's import-path fix on fix/pylint-ci with a real pytest run (not just pylint). 6 tests fail with 'Cannot connect to DAZ Studio' / ConnectionError: test_daz_load_file_merge, test_daz_load_file_not_found, test_daz_save_scene_copy_ok, test_daz_save_scene_copy_sends_correct_body, test_daz_save_scene_copy_dirty_scene, test_daz_save_scene_copy_does_not_use_script_registry. Root cause: daz_save_scene_copy/daz_load_file route through get_scene()/run_dazpy() in src/vangard_daz_mcp/_client.py, which uses a separate DazClient/DazScene singleton from the httpx client that respx mocks via set_http_client() -- so these 'mocked' tests silently fall through to a real DazClient and try to reach a live DazScriptServer at localhost:18811. This is the exact same gap already diagnosed and fixed on phase4_tools_implementation via commit 4712f41 ('fix(tests): repair broken test-suite imports and dazpy mocking gap'), which added set_scene()/set_daz_client() to _client.py plus a mock_scene fixture in test_server.py -- but that fix never made it onto fix/pylint-ci (separate fork point from master, same root cause as daz-mcp-server-zp7/ful). Not something introduced by ful's import-path fix -- pre-existing on this branch. Fix: port 4712f41's set_scene()/set_daz_client() additions and the mock_scene fixture rewrite from phase4_tools_implementation onto fix/pylint-ci (or merge the branches).
acceptance_criteria: pytest tests/test_server.py passes without a live DAZ Studio connection.
notes: See daz-mcp-server-ful's investigation notes and daz-mcp-server-zp7 for the related import-path half of this same divergence.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/pylint-ci branch (commit 8515a26). Ported the fix from phase4_tools_implementation's commit 4712f41 (same root divergence as zp7/ful -- fix/pylint-ci forked before that commit landed). Added set_scene() to _client.py so tests can inject a test double for the DazScene singleton, and an autouse MagicMock mock_scene fixture in test_server.py; rewrote the 6 affected tests (test_daz_load_file_merge, test_daz_load_file_not_found, test_daz_save_scene_copy_ok/sends_correct_path/dirty_scene/connect_error/does_not_use_script_registry) to mock at the get_scene() boundary instead of expecting HTTP-level mocking. Verified locally: all 74 tests in test_server.py pass with no live DAZ Studio connection; pytest --collect-only still collects 441 tests; no-member/no-name-in-module remains 10.00/10.

title: DazBusyError/StudioBusyError/ConcurrencyLimitError don't exist in any published dazpy release yet
description: Discovered while investigating pylint no-member findings for daz-mcp-server-ful. src/vangard_daz_mcp/_errors.py:39 does 'isinstance(exc, daz_exc.DazBusyError)' as part of the studio-busy-handling feature (merged via PR #4 / commit 906cd88 'feat: surface DazBusyError as a clear ToolError to MCP tool callers'), and tests/test_errors.py references daz_exc.StudioBusyError and daz_exc.ConcurrencyLimitError. None of these three names exist in dazpy.exceptions in any version currently on PyPI (checked up through 2.7.2, the latest published as of this writing; pyproject.toml pins dazpy>=2.6.0). Per report, DazBusyError ships in daz-script-server 2.8.0, which has not been published to PyPI yet -- this whole feature was built/tested against a pre-release dazpy. Effect: _errors.py:39 will raise AttributeError the moment handle_dazpy_error() runs against ANY exception in a real deployment (attribute lookup happens at call time), and tests/test_errors.py's three busy-error tests fail at collection/run time with AttributeError since dazpy.exceptions.StudioBusyError doesn't exist. Fix: once dazpy 2.8.0 (or whichever version actually ships DazBusyError) is published, bump pyproject.toml's dazpy>=2.6.0 pin to require it, and reconcile test_errors.py's StudioBusyError/ConcurrencyLimitError names with _errors.py's actual DazBusyError (single class vs two, matching whatever the real dazpy 2.8.0 API turns out to be).
acceptance_criteria: pyproject.toml requires a dazpy version that actually publishes DazBusyError; _errors.py and test_errors.py use matching, real exception class names; pylint --enable=no-member src/vangard_daz_mcp/_errors.py tests/test_errors.py reports zero findings.
notes: Blocked on an external dependency (dazpy/daz-script-server 2.8.0 publication to PyPI) -- not fixable purely within this repo until that ships.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/pylint-ci branch (commit d4dbe50). dazpy 2.8.0 -- which publishes DazBusyError, StudioBusyError, and ConcurrencyLimitError -- was tagged and released to PyPI (bluemoonfoundry/daz-script-server v2.8.0 tag pushed, release workflow completed successfully). Bumped pyproject.toml's dazpy>=2.6.0 pin to dazpy>=2.8.0. Verified against the real published 2.8.0 wheel: pylint --enable=no-member on _errors.py and test_errors.py is clean (10.00/10), and all 7 tests in test_errors.py pass. Whole-repo no-member/no-name-in-module is now 10.00/10 (zero findings) -- this was the last outstanding item from daz-mcp-server-ful's investigation.

title: pylint: resolve redefined-outer-name findings (190, likely pytest fixtures)
description:
190 redefined-outer-name findings, per the baseline in epic daz-mcp-server-lkb. Almost certainly pytest fixtures being used as test-function parameters -- the correct, idiomatic pytest pattern (see tests/conftest.py live_client, figure_label, etc.), not a real defect. Depends on daz-mcp-server-0t0's decision, but this category is the strongest candidate in the whole findings list for 'disable the check, don't fix the code' -- spend a few minutes confirming the hypothesis (sample the findings) before writing any fixes, since the likely right outcome here is a one-line config change, not per-instance work.

Run: pylint --disable=all --enable=redefined-outer-name on the repo's python files to confirm the pattern.
close_reason: Already resolved by daz-mcp-server-0t0's config change (commit bdfadcc on fix/pylint-ci): confirmed all 190 hits were the pytest-fixture-as-parameter idiom (100% in tests/, 0 in src/), and pylint.yml already scopes --disable=redefined-outer-name to tests/. Verified: 'pylint --disable=all --enable=redefined-outer-name' on src/ scores 10.00/10 (zero hits), and the actual CI-configured tests/ command produces zero redefined-outer-name findings.

title: pylint: audit unused-argument findings (354)
description:
354 unused-argument findings, per the baseline in epic daz-mcp-server-lkb. Depends on daz-mcp-server-0t0, which calls for a sample audit before deciding scope -- likely dominated by two false-positive patterns: (a) mcp.tool() function parameters whose signature is dictated by the tool schema rather than internal logic, (b) pytest fixture parameters requested only for side effects/skip behavior.

Approach: sample ~20-30 findings across src/vangard_daz_mcp/tools and tests to categorize real-vs-false-positive ratio, then either (a) add targeted pylint disable comments with a one-line reason on the genuine false positives, or (b) if the ratio is overwhelmingly false-positive, disable the check for the relevant directories/patterns via config instead of hundreds of inline comments.

Run: pylint --disable=all --enable=unused-argument on the repo's python files for an isolated list.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/pylint-ci branch (commit f781e41). Audited all ~10 src/ + integration_test.py unused-argument findings individually (tests/ 344 hits already handled by 0t0's scoped pylint.yml disable). 7 confirmed genuine false positives (FastMCP lifespan signature, three already-documented 'reserved for future' / 'not yet implemented' tool params, and two test-suite functions kept for a uniform callback signature) -- added inline '# pylint: disable=unused-argument' with a one-line reason at each. 3 were real defects masquerading as unused params (daz_get_scene_layout/daz_find_nearby_nodes's include_types filter and daz_batch_select's add_to_selection never actually implemented despite being documented) -- filed as daz-mcp-server-skr and daz-mcp-server-i2l instead of silencing them, left the pylint warning live since it's correctly flagging incomplete code. Verified locally: src/ isolated unused-argument count drops from ~10 to exactly the 3 filed bugs.

title: pylint: add missing docstrings (387 function + 99 class + 5 module = 491)
description:
491 missing-function-docstring/missing-class-docstring/missing-module-docstring findings across the repo, per the baseline in epic daz-mcp-server-lkb. Depends on daz-mcp-server-0t0 decision on whether this check stays enabled at all (a valid alternative outcome of that issue is disabling it project-wide rather than writing ~500 docstrings) -- if kept enabled, this issue is where the actual docstring-writing work happens.

Suggested approach if proceeding: prioritize src/vangard_daz_mcp/tools/ public @mcp.tool() functions first (user/LLM-facing API surface where docstrings genuinely help), then internal helpers, then tests/ last (test docstrings are lowest value; consider excluding tests/ from this check instead).

Run: pylint --disable=all --enable=missing-function-docstring,missing-class-docstring,missing-module-docstring on the repo's python files for an isolated list.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/pylint-ci branch (commit 696b859). 491 findings (387 function + 99 class + 5 module) broke down as: 12 in src/, 12 in integration_test.py, and 467 (95%) in tests/. All @mcp.tool() functions already had full docstrings -- the LLM-facing API surface this check protects was already covered. Wrote real one-line docstrings for the 24 src/+integration_test.py hits (singleton accessors, main(), 5 tool submodule docstrings, and each test_* suite function). For tests/'s 467 hits -- confirmed self-descriptively-named test_* functions and TestXxx grouping classes -- extended pylint.yml's existing tests/-scoped disable list (from 0t0/91s) with missing-function-docstring/missing-class-docstring; module docstrings remain required everywhere including tests/. Verified locally: src/ isolated docstring score 10.00/10 (zero hits); the CI-configured tests/ command produces zero missing-*-docstring findings.

title: pylint.yml: trim Python version matrix to match requires-python
description:
pylint.yml's build matrix runs python-version ["3.8", "3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12"], but pyproject.toml declares requires-python = ">=3.11". The project doesn't claim to support 3.8-3.10 anywhere else (uses PEP 604 unions like 'list[str] | None' throughout, which is fine for pylint's astroid parser but signals the project's actual target), so three of the five CI matrix legs are testing versions the project isn't meant to run on at all -- wasted CI time and a source of version-specific noise unrelated to real code quality.

Fix: trim the matrix to ["3.11", "3.12"] to match the declared support window (add 3.13 too if the team wants to track it, otherwise keep to the two currently-declared-supported minors).

Discovered alongside daz-mcp-server-wdk while investigating why the pylint CI check has never passed since it was added (2026-05-08).
close_reason: Fixed on fix/pylint-ci branch (commit ad02f64): trimmed pylint.yml's build matrix from [3.8, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12] to [3.11, 3.12] to match pyproject.toml's requires-python >=3.11.

title: Bring daz-mcp-server to real pylint compliance
description:
The Pylint CI check (.github/workflows/pylint.yml) has failed on every push to master since it was added on 2026-05-08 -- confirmed via 'gh run list --branch master' showing failures on every recorded run. It currently reports 'Your code has been rated at 3.46/10', but that number is itself misleading: the workflow only runs 'pip install pylint' before analysis, never installing the project's own dependencies (httpx, fastmcp, dazpy, pytest, etc.), so pylint can't resolve any third-party import anywhere in the codebase. Reinstalling properly (uv venv + pip install -e . + dev deps) and re-running locally gives a truer baseline of 4.41/10 with this category breakdown across the whole repo (git ls-files '*.py'):

  387 missing-function-docstring     58 broad-exception-caught
  354 unused-argument                41 unused-import
  190 redefined-outer-name           21 protected-access
  158 no-name-in-module              16 duplicate-code
   99 missing-class-docstring        15 import-outside-toplevel
   79 line-too-long                  10 too-many-arguments
   67 no-member                      10 too-many-positional-arguments
                                      10 superfluous-parens
                                       8 invalid-name
                                       6 global-statement
                                       5 missing-module-docstring
                                       4 unsubscriptable-object

This is a codebase that has never been pylint-clean since the check was introduced -- the workflow was added without ever bringing the code up to its default ruleset or tuning that ruleset to the project's actual conventions (e.g. pytest fixture patterns necessarily trigger 'redefined-outer-name' and 'unused-argument' by design, which is not a real defect). Discovered while working on the DazBusyError busy-handling PR (#4) when its CI checks came back failing for reasons entirely unrelated to that PR's 2-file diff.

Goal: a CI gate that (a) actually reflects real code quality rather than environment misconfiguration, and (b) the team can trust as a real signal going forward, achieved by fixing the two mechanical CI bugs, deciding + applying sane config tuning for convention-mismatch checks, and then working through the remaining real findings by category.

This epic is closed once all its child issues (CI fixes, config tuning decision, and each finding-category task) are closed.

title: Test suite imports broken across 17 files after server.py refactor split
description: Commit 2e9fbbf (feat(refactor): split 15K-line server.py into 13 focused tool modules, 2026-06-26) split the monolithic server.py into tools/*.py + _mcp.py + _client.py + _registry.py, but the test suite was never updated. 17 of 18 files under tests/ still do 'from vangard_daz_mcp.server import (...)' expecting ~130 names (nearly every tool function, plus _register_scripts, CONTENT_BROWSER_URL, and module state _http_client/_content_browser_client) that no longer live in server.py -- it is now a 15-line entrypoint. This breaks pytest collection for the entire tests/ directory (conftest.py fails to import, which cascades to every test file via fixture discovery). Discovered while implementing the DazBusyError MCP-side wiring (feature/studio-busy-handling branch) -- worked around there with pytest --noconftest on an isolated new test file, but the pre-existing suite itself needs a real fix. Two options considered but not decided: (1) restore ~130 re-exports in server.py (one file, minimal diff, restores tests' existing assumption), or (2) rewrite each of the 17 test files' imports to point at the correct submodule (vangard_daz_mcp.tools.camera_light, .scene, ._registry, ._client, etc. -- more files touched but keeps the refactor's module boundaries clean). May already be partially addressed by in-progress uncommitted work on phase4_tools_implementation (dirty changes to morph.py and test_actors_integration.py at time of discovery) -- check that branch's state before starting.
close_reason: Already fixed by commit 4712f41 (fix(tests): repair broken test-suite imports and dazpy mocking gap), which is an ancestor of phase4_tools_implementation. Verified: pytest --collect-only now collects 453 tests with zero import errors; all 17 test files import from correct submodules (.tools.*, ._client, ._registry) instead of the old vangard_daz_mcp.server.

Macro recording, daz_get_performance_stats, daz_explain_last_error, daz_script_help, daz_validate_script are pure-Python MCP-server features and out of scope.

title: Add daz_save_scene_copy using POST /scene/save-copy endpoint

Add a new daz_save_scene_copy(path) MCP tool that calls this endpoint and returns {ok, path, source, method}. title: daz_batch_select: add_to_selection=False never clears the prior selection

acceptance_criteria: include_types either filters results as documented, or the docstrings/examples no longer claim it does.

title: pylint: review duplicate-code findings (16)
description:
16 duplicate-code (R0801) findings, per the baseline in epic daz-mcp-server-lkb. Likely a natural consequence of the many structurally-similar mcp.tool() wrapper functions (payload-build + try/post/check_response + except/handle_network_error pattern, repeated across tools/) and similar pytest fixture patterns across test files -- not necessarily a real defect, but worth a look at whether shared helper extraction would genuinely improve maintainability vs. just being inherent to having many independently-necessary, thin async endpoint wrappers.

Decide per-instance: extract a shared helper where it clearly helps, or raise pylint's min-similarity-lines / disable R0801 for the specific repeated patterns that are an accepted tradeoff of the architecture.

Run: pylint --disable=all --enable=duplicate-code on the repo's python files for an isolated list.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/pylint-ci branch (commit 6e1b1b2). Reviewed all 16 duplicate-code findings individually per the issue's own suggested approach. Two were genuine substantial duplication, extracted into shared code: _EMOTION_DEFINITIONS (~100-line dict, byte-identical in tools/morph.py and tools/cinematic.py) moved to new src/vangard_daz_mcp/_emotions.py; and _mcp.py's _execute()/tools/utility.py's daz_execute()/daz_execute_file() shared payload+error-handling logic consolidated into two new _mcp.py helpers (_execute_payload, _execute_raw) while preserving each function's distinct return shape. The remaining 12 pairs matched the issue's own hypothesis -- the try/except run_dazpy() wrapper repeated by architecture across nearly every dazpy-routed tool -- confirmed by testing that raising pylint's min-similarity-lines from 4 to 8 collapses 11 of them to zero; added that threshold to pyproject.toml's [tool.pylint.similarities] with rationale. The one survivor (conftest.py vs test_phase5_integration.py fixtures, ~50 lines) is a pre-existing SKILL_DEVELOPMENT.md-documented deliberate choice -- added a targeted inline disable instead of raising the threshold further. Verified locally: duplicate-code is 10.00/10; unused-import/no-member/no-name-in-module/protected-access remain 10.00/10 (no regressions); pytest --collect-only collects 441 tests; test_server.py + test_wardrobe.py (89 tests) pass.

title: Pylint CI check has never passed since it was added (score 3.46/10)
description:
The Pylint GitHub Actions check (pylint.yml, added 2026-05-08 in commit 'Create pylint.yml') has failed on every push to master since it was introduced -- confirmed via gh run list --branch master showing failures on 2026-05-08, 2026-06-27, and 2026-07-02, i.e. it has never once passed.

Two distinct root causes observed on PR #4 (feature/studio-busy-handling):
1. ~90 import-error (E0401) findings across the repo (httpx, fastmcp, dazpy, pytest, etc.) -- the pylint.yml workflow appears to run pylint without installing the project's dependencies first, so pylint can't resolve any third-party import. This alone tanks the score regardless of actual code quality.
2. Widespread duplicate-code (R0801) findings across tools/*.py and tests/*.py (e.g. tools/animation.py vs tools/spatial.py, tools/spatial.py vs tools/transform.py, test_wardrobe.py vs test_server.py) -- likely a natural consequence of the many structurally-similar @mcp.tool() wrapper functions and test fixtures across 13 tool modules, not necessarily a real defect, but pylint's default duplicate-code threshold flags it heavily.

Net effect: 'Your code has been rated at 3.46/10' and the check fails on every PR regardless of what that PR actually changes, making the CI gate meaningless as a real signal. Any future PR (like #4) inherits pre-existing failures it didn't cause.

Fix should start with (1) -- installing project dependencies in the pylint.yml workflow before running pylint -- since that's a clear, mechanical CI config bug. (2) may need either fixing (shared helper extraction) or explicitly tuning pylint's duplicate-code settings/min-similarity-lines if the duplication is an accepted tradeoff of the tools/*.py structure.
close_reason: Superseded by a proper breakdown: epic + CI-fix issues + per-category systematic-fix issues, created for a fresh session.

title: migrate wardrobe.py: 2 tools onto DazGeometry

acceptance_criteria: daz_set_keyframe routes through DazProperty.set_key instead of the registered script.
notes: From the 2026-07-12 dazpy migration audit. Smallest possible migration task -- one tool.

title: migrate scene.py: 4 tools onto DazScene, and re-check checkpoint fidelity
description: daz_scene_info -> DazScene.scene_snapshot() (direct). daz_get_node_hierarchy -> DazScene.node_tree (direct). daz_save_scene_state/daz_restore_scene_state -> composable via scene_snapshot()/DazSkeleton.snapshot(), which may capture individual bone transforms that the current registered-script checkpoint does NOT (it only captures root-level transforms + morphs per skeleton, not per-bone -- confirmed today while adding cleanup fixtures to test_phase5_integration.py::TestResetPose). Check dazpy's snapshot depth before rewriting; if it does cover bone-level state, this migration also closes a real safety gap in the live-integration test suite, not just a code-quality one.
acceptance_criteria: All 4 tools route through dazpy. If DazSkeleton.snapshot()/scene_snapshot() captures per-bone transforms, daz_save_scene_state/daz_restore_scene_state docstrings and the test-suite cleanup fixtures added 2026-07-12 (test_phase5_integration.py, test_actors_integration.py) are updated to rely on full restoration instead of the reset-to-known-baseline workaround.
notes: From the 2026-07-12 dazpy migration audit. Highest-value item in scene.py because of the safety-gap angle, not just code cleanliness.
close_reason: Migrated daz_scene_info/daz_get_node_hierarchy/daz_save_scene_state/daz_restore_scene_state onto new dazpy primitives (DazScene.overview/node_hierarchy, DazSceneState). Closes the bone-level checkpoint gap flagged in the original ticket. Also found and fixed a real ERC-inflation bug (raw vs computed value) at the dazpy level (DazProperty.raw_value, DazPose fix) plus in the registered-script checkpoint before the primitive migration. Removed 4 now-dead registered scripts. Updated test fixtures (test_actors_integration.py, test_phase5_integration.py) to use full checkpoint restore instead of the reset-to-baseline workaround. Verified live: 33/33 non-skipped actor tests + 5/5 TestResetPose + 73/73 mocked server tests pass.

title: migrate cinematic.py: 21 tools onto camera/light/skeleton/keyframe primitives
description: The most composite module in the codebase -- shot sequences, storyboards, choreography, focus pulls, atmosphere. All 21 non-blocked tools are Python orchestration on top of primitives dazpy already exposes (DazCamera, DazLight, DazSkeleton, DazProperty.set_key, DazNode.snapshot/scene_snapshot). Full list: daz_create_shot_sequence, daz_animate_conversation, daz_create_scene, daz_animate_camera_movement, daz_create_camera_path, daz_create_character_path, daz_arrange_characters, daz_choreograph_action, daz_animate_light, daz_create_light_sequence, daz_plan_shot, daz_create_storyboard, daz_set_focus_point, daz_animate_focus_pull, daz_set_scene_atmosphere, daz_apply_visual_style, daz_export_node_config, daz_import_node_config, daz_time_expression, daz_sync_character_beats.
acceptance_criteria: Each tool rewritten to build on dazpy primitives instead of a registered DazScript string. daz_setup_shot_coverage and daz_create_camera_rig are explicitly NOT included -- blocked on the node-creation gap tracked in daz-script-server. Given the size, this can be split into smaller PRs by sub-area (shot/storyboard, choreography, lighting/atmosphere) rather than done as one change.
notes: From the 2026-07-12 dazpy migration audit. Largest single module in the codebase by tool count (23 total, 21 migratable).

title: Phase 6.6: Scene export — write FBX or OBJ from selected nodes
description: No export tools exist. Many pipelines (game engines, VFX) need geometry out of DAZ. Add: daz_export_fbx(node_labels, output_path, options) → exports the named nodes to FBX via DzExportMgr with format 'Filmbox'; daz_export_obj(node_labels, output_path, options) → exports to Wavefront OBJ. Options include: include_morphs (bool), apply_current_pose (bool), scale_factor (float). Use DzExportMgr.doExport(filename, exporterName, settings) pattern. Gracefully return an error if the required exporter is not installed.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add daz_search_content integrating daz-content-browser vector search
description: The daz-content-browser project runs a FastAPI server with POST /api/v1/search for semantic vector search over the installed DAZ product catalog (BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 embeddings, ChromaDB). Also has POST /api/v1/scene/load to load a .duf by absolute path (delegates to daz-script-server). Add two MCP tools: (1) daz_search_content(query: str, max_results: int = 10) — calls content browser POST /api/v1/search and returns product list with sku, name, description, compatible_figures, tags, store_url. (2) daz_load_product(product_name: str) — calls /api/v1/products?q=name then /api/v1/scene/load. Content browser URL configurable via DAZ_CONTENT_BROWSER_URL env var (default http://localhost:8080). Use a separate httpx client (not the DAZ script server client). Skip gracefully if content browser is not reachable. Add mock tests.
close_reason: Implemented daz_search_content and daz_load_product with separate httpx client, graceful fallback, and 14 mock tests all passing

title: pylint: address remaining smaller-count categories
description:
Remaining smaller categories from the baseline in epic daz-mcp-server-lkb, bundled together since each is individually small: import-outside-toplevel (15), too-many-arguments (10), too-many-positional-arguments (10), superfluous-parens (10), invalid-name (8), global-statement (6), unsubscriptable-object (4). About 63 findings total.

Mostly mechanical (superfluous-parens, invalid-name) or small design calls (too-many-arguments may indicate a function doing too much, or may be an accepted mcp.tool() signature shape; global-statement and import-outside-toplevel may be intentional patterns in _mcp.py's lifespan/singleton setup). Sample each sub-category before deciding fix-vs-accept; split into separate issues if any one of these turns out to be bigger or more contentious than expected once actually looked at.

Run: pylint --disable=all --enable=import-outside-toplevel,too-many-arguments,too-many-positional-arguments,superfluous-parens,invalid-name,global-statement,unsubscriptable-object on the repo's python files for an isolated list.
